chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: First seeing the Booker T. Washington Community Center Band parade
summary: At nine or ten, after the family moved to 10th Street, he saw the all-kid band in a parade; Dickie Wells was in it, and he mentions Bill Beason, who later replaced Chick Webb and went with John Kirby.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: the band by that time, and I had gotten into the band. I was getting a little ahead of my story, because --

-- the first time I knew anything was we moved from 15th Street to 10th Street. Now I'm about nine years old, nine or ten years old, and then I never paid any attention to music. I hadn't even heard anything about music before that. There used to be a band on the corner that would play, a brass band, adult band, and sometimes I'd hear them rehearse on a Saturday, something like that. But I never paid any attention to it.
But one day, getting into how I got into it, I went down to -- they let me go down to the corner, to see the parade, at Walnut Street and 10th. We were living on 10th then.

And I'd go down, and I went down to look at the band and listen to the parade and looking at the band, and then I saw this Booker T. Washington Community Center Band, and it was all kids, you know, all youngsters. And Dickie Wells, he was there.
This is the Booker T. Washington Community--
Yeah, right. All these guys, Bill Beason and all of them, you know. I don't think Beason had come yet. I think I went in before Beason. But Dickie was there.
Drums. He played -- when Chick died, he took his place.
Also, when Ne'll Spencer died in John Kirby's band, he went with John Kirby.
What's he doing now, do you know?
I don't know. I've seen him once, in about 12 years.
